prefinal exam"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u0026nbsp;I have tried to answer some of the questions regarding case discussion of our patient\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;1. How to clinically differentiate between coarse and fine crepitations ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns-\u0026nbsp; well, crepitations or crackles\u0026nbsp; are adventitious respiratory sounds which occur when an obstructed airway due to accumulated\u0026nbsp; secretions opens in inspiratory phase.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe sudden opening of an obstructed airway causes an immediate re-equilibration of the pressures on both sides creating vibrations in the airway walls.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFine crackles --\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA).\u0026nbsp; having a short duration and a higher pitch,\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Often, fine crackles are repetitive, originate\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; in the basal part of the lung, and not altered\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; by coughing.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB) Coarse crackles\u0026nbsp; appear to be a longer\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;duration and a\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;lower pitch.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;There is no specific location from where\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; coarse crackles primarily originate. They are\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; often altered by coughing.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5834319\/#:~:text=Bronchial%20breath%20sounds%20are%20blasting,of%20pneumonia%20or%20pulmonary%20fibrosis.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5834319\/#:~:text=Bronchial%20breath%20sounds%20are%20blasting,of%20pneumonia%20or%20pulmonary%20fibrosis.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Why are bronchial\u0026nbsp; breath sounds heard in lung fields on ascultation in this case and how to clinically differentiate between normal vesicular ans bronchial breath sounds?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns-- Bronchial breath sounds in the lung fields are heard in our patient due to consolidation secondary to hospital acquired pneumonia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003ENormal vesicular breath sounds are :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESoft, low pitched, and rustling in quality\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; a) Inspiratory phase remains\u0026nbsp; longer than the\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; expiratory phase\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; b)\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Inspiration is higher pitch than expiration\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;c) No pause between inspiration and expiration\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBronchial breath sounds :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is loud, hollow, and high pitch\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EExpiratory phase is longer than inspiratory phase\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is distinct pause between inspiration and expiration due to absent alveolar phase\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4518345\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4518345\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Management of the case and role of ECMO?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAns :- fluconazole for oral candidiasis is being given, doxycycline also given\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EECMO -Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation consists of a circuit where blood is drained through a catheter from the venous vascular system, circulated in a pump outside the body, and reinfused into the other venous or arterial vascular system depending on the ECMO circuit type for circulation in the body.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe ECMO machine performs the function of the lungs successfully so the lungs can rest and we can use very low settings on the breathing machine. This protects the lungs from additional damage that the high pressures from the breathing machine cause.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/7262898614720184852\/posts\/default\/4049811853488427713"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/7262898614720184852\/posts\/default\/4049811853488427713"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/180pashikantimadhav.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/osce-prefinal-exam.html","title":"osce prefinal exam"}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"P Madhav"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/09349085159537126519"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}]},{"id":{"$t":"tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-7262898614720184852.post-2730943466490321885"},"published":{"$t":"2023-12-05T05:24:00.000-08:00"},"updated":{"$t":"2023-12-05T07:20:54.013-08:00"},"title":{"type":"text","$t":"Prefinal long case-83 yr old male with shortness of breath with pneumonia "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"I'am P .madhav, a medical student. This is an E-Log , that depicts the patient centered approach for learning medicine. This has been done after taking consent from patient and their relatives. Here , we discuss our individual patient's problems through online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an a online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient\/ attender was informed the purpose of the information being acquired. An informed consent was taken from patient\/ attender and there is omission of information that was requested to be omitted.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 83yr old male came with complaints of shortness of breath since 15 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu style=\"font-style: italic;\"\u003Echief complaints:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECough since 14 days\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFever since 12 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eshortness of breath since 15 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHistory of Presenting illness:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was admitted to ICU on 20\/11\/23 in the morning at 10 am with breathlessness. It was insidious in onset and gradually progressive, continuous and present during rest ( patient was feeling breathless even upon walking to washroom) with no associated relieving factors. Patient's attender also complained of awakening during night due to breathlessness. No h\/o palpitations, stridor, or hoarseness of voice\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatients attender also told abt cough which was insidious in onset, gradually progressive associated with sputum which was white in colour ,scanty amount, mucoid in consistency and non foul smelling\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient also complained of intermittent spikes of fever since 12 days( 4 times a day ), associated with chills and rigors, not relieved on taking medication and not associated with headache, vomiting\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;No h\/o chest pain, orthopnea, PND\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o recurrent sore throat or cold\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o loss of consciousness,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of similar complaints in the past\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is N\/K\/C\/O of Hypertension, Diabetes mellitus, TB, Epilepsy, Bronchial asthma, Thyroid disorders\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o blood transfusions and surgeries\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EFAMILY HISTORY: \u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003EInsignificant\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eas mentioned by the attender\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet - Mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite - decreased\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep- Adequate\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and Bladder movements- Regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddiction - consumption of alcohol occasionally,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;h\/o smoking since 30 yrs (3 packs per day) reduced to 1 pack per day since 2 yrs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EGENERAL :\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003ERESPIRATORY SYSTEM :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUpper respiratory tract
